lines: Ever noticed airplane windows are never square?
The Comet was the world's first jet airliner.
It flew higher and faster than anything before it.
But in 1954, two of them broke apart in mid-air.
So engineers put a whole Comet in a giant water tank,
and pressurized it again and again.
See, every flight, the cabin puffs up a little,
then shrinks back down when you land.
And all that stress piles up in the sharp corners.
Thousands of flights later, the metal cracks.
Round windows spread that stress out evenly.
So that's why your window is round.
And that tiny hole in the window?
It balances the air pressure between the panes, so the outer one takes all the load.
